en: Praise of the Self-Existent One: Homage to you who possess the universal form; homage to you whose form is light.
Homage eternal to the Self-Existent One, the cause of the world’s deliverance. (1)

You are the Buddha, you are the Dharma, you are the son of the One Possessing the Ten Powers, and likewise the Bodhisattva; you are the monk, you are the disciple, you are the bearer of the supreme vajra, and likewise the Dharmadhātu.
You are Brahmā, you are Viṣṇu, you are the Lord of the Pramatha hosts, you are Mahendra, and you are Yama.
You are Varuṇa, you are the Lord of Wealth, you are Fire and Wind, you are Nirṛti, and you are Maheśvara. ||2||
You are the spirits, the departed, and the state of animals; you are the immortals, Aditi, and the oceans; you are we, and you alone are the fourfold womb of birth.
You are the body of the three qualities, the singular embodiment of the five knowledges;
you are the castes, time, the months, the day, and the night; you alone are the five elements.
O you who are food, jewel, and everything, whose intellect is ever great, we always bow down to you. || 3 ||
By means of the fivefold knowledge, you yourself create the Buddhas as well as the Bodhisattvas; these five elements, the three qualities (guṇas), Hari, Giriśa, and all things mobile and immobile.
Abiding in the hearts of all, you cause everything to dance, and you are the protector everywhere.
You are the seed, you are the sprout, and you are the fruit as well as the tree; we bow to you at all times.

O Blessed One, you alone prevail over the most excellent Kṣatriya power here; you distribute all the gods, villages, sacred fords, regions, kings along with their subjects, and even all the merchants.
You also apportion the entire distribution of the luminaries across other continents as well.
You are the single lamp that has become the seed, pervading this entire world; we bow to you. || 5 ||
Your light, spreading all around—white, reddish, dark, yellow, and red—is seen; therefore, we consider this entire world to be you, and we bow to you eternally.
Those men who shall recite this hymn composed by the Great King, having attained the status of a universal monarch (cakravartin), shall indeed obtain liberation. || 7 ||
